title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability incident follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync to review the reliability incidents observed last week (timeouts, spikes of 5xxs, and client-side rate limiting), align on investigation findings, and agree next steps: logs/traces handoff, focused stress test, retry/backoff tuning, and schedule a deeper SE run. Customer flagged a repeat of 500s at peak, and saw elevated P99 latency. Redwood proposed short-term mitigations and longer-term routing and autoscaling checks.
topics: Next steps: logs, benchmarks, SE deep-dive
action_items: Liam O'Connor - Share curated prod traces (request IDs, ingress timestamps, and backend latencies) - 2026-05-12
Priya Singh - Run focused 1000-request stress test simulating peak traffic and upload results to shared folder - 2026-05-14
Sara Patel - Implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter and validate against 5xx simulation - 2026-05-13
next_steps: Send trimmed set of logs and traces (Liam)
Run targeted load test from customer infra (Priya)
Adjust retry/backoff and re-run P95 latency checks (Sara)
Schedule SE deep-dive for model routing and tokenization impact (by 2026-05-16)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Sara Patel (Redwood SE), Mason Reed (CTO - Atlas), Priya Singh (SRE), Carlos Diaz (Product)

[00:00] Liam (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda - incident recap, what we saw in logs, short-term mitigations, and then next steps. Priya, do you want to kick off with what you observed?

[02:15] Priya (Customer SRE): Yeah, sure. So last Wednesday around 14:30 our app started seeing a burst of request failures; roughly 2% of requests flipped to 500s over a 10-minute window, and P99 latency climbed to about 2.8s from a baseline 1.1s. We correlated with our frontend traces and saw long tails hitting the inference endpoint. We've attached example request IDs in the ticket.

[05:00] Sara (Redwood SE): Thanks, that's helpful. From our side we saw a mix of timeouts and a small number of 5xxs originating at the runtime layer. The pattern looks like sudden queue growth then some workers hitting OOM/evictions - could be a batch-sizing edge or a KV cache miss storm, maybe due to prefix cache churn. Also saw some client retries amplifying load.

[07:30] Mason (CTO): When you say "KV cache miss storm", do you mean the K-V cash, like the cached prefixes? I just want to be sure it's not a network problem on our side.

[08:05] Sara: Yeah, sorry the auto-transcript's weird - I mean KV cache, as in the key-value cache in the serving runtime. That can cause higher token compute if misses spike. We also saw a handful of 502/503s that line up with autoscaler events.

[12:30] Carlos (Product): We did push a config change that increased concurrency on the client for latency, so we may have pushed into a regime where client concurrency plus retries created a feedback loop. We thought retries were backoff limited but perhaps not.

[15:00] Liam: Ok so three candidate contributors: 1) client-side concurrency + insufficient backoff causing spikes, 2) KV cache churn increasing per-request compute, and 3) autoscaler cold-starts or fractional capacity causing brief 5xx windows. We need to confirm. Priya, can you run the focused stress test Sara recommended? 1k requests simulating peak plus retries.

[18:20] Priya: Yep we can run that. Question - what's the suggested retry/backoff policy? We're using a simple fixed retry with 200ms interval right now.

[19:05] Sara: Strong suggestion to move to exponential backoff with jitter; start with base 200ms, cap at 2s, and do at most 3 retries. Also enable client-side throttling when you see 429s or rising latencies, and prefer idempotent callers to use a token bucket limiter. We'll share a sample config.

[22:00] Mason: Does Redwood's hosted service expose server-side rate limit headers we can use to adapt?

[22:45] Liam: Yes - we include x-rdwd-rate-limit and x-rdwd-rate-remaining headers in responses for hosted; for dedicated you can also surface those via the proxy. We'll send details.

[25:10] Priya: On the autoscaling note, we saw a scale-up event around the spike time but there were a few minutes of increased queueing before capacity fully came online. Is there a way to reduce the cold-start/scale latency?

[26:00] Sara: A couple options: pre-warm worker pools, use reserved capacity (Dedicated) for steady workloads, or tweak the autoscaler aggressiveness. For this POC we're running on shared hosted; we can simulate reserved-like behavior by pinning a small pool for the test. Also we can tune the keep-alive / warm-up settings so that new workers load the model faster. We'll put recommended values in the follow-up doc.

[31:00] Carlos: Are any of these suggestions likely to change model output or cost materially? Our product team is sensitive to token cost.

[31:40] Sara: Cache churn and rerunning long prefixes will increase cost per request temporarily; pre-warming increases cost but reduces tail latency. On dedicated, you trade higher fixed cost for lower tail and more predictable P95/P99. We'll quantify during the focused benchmark.

[34:10] Priya: For the logs, what exactly do you need from us beyond the request IDs? We can share traces but need to redact PII.

[34:40] Liam: Prefer: request IDs, ingress timestamps, client-side latencies, any proxy logs around the time window, and a sample of full request payloads (redacted). We'll provide an S3 upload link and a short template for the fields. Aim to send a trimmed set not the whole long tail.

[37:05] Sara: One more quick observation - we saw some 5xx responses with an internal error string referencing "kernel selection" in the runtime logs; could be a rare combination of sequence length + batch that triggers an edge. We'll try to reproduce in our test rig. If we can reproduce, we can patch the kernel selection fallback or add a safety guard.

[40:30] Mason: Great. If we can't reproduce, what's the escalation path? We need an SLA-style incident follow-up.

[41:00] Liam: We'll treat this as high-priority for the POC. Next steps: we'll gather traces, SE will run deterministic reproduce tests, and we'll propose a mitigation (retry/backoff + temporary client throttle) within 48 hours. If it's reproducible we'll schedule a code-level fix timeline. We'll also create a short postmortem draft.

[44:10] Liam: Quick recap of action items and owners - I'll send the upload link and request template; Priya will run the stress test; Sara will implement client-side retry samples and run reproduce tests; Carlos and Mason will coordinate internal stakeholders. We'll sync again after the tests, earlier if we hit a reproducible failure. Thanks everyone.

[44:50] End of call.
